summary: Mission Walk is a below-market-rate condominium development at 330 and 335 Berry St: SocketSite (Oct 27, 2008) reported applications for its 131 BMR condos across both addresses, for buyers earning up to 80-100% of area median income, with applications due January 22, 2009 and a lottery scheduled for January 28, 2009; this building (330 Berry St) was completed in 2009 per DataSF Assessor records.

milestones.text: Below-market-rate purchase applications open for the 131 condo units at 330/335 Berry St ahead of a January 2009 lottery, while the buildings are still under construction

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Production and Conservation Business Center (Geospatial Enterprise Operations), NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service
images.license_note: USDA's data.gov catalog record for NAIP imagery (published by the Farm Production and Conservation Business Center) sets the license to the U.S. government public-domain label (usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0). Read 2026-09-22; publisher name re-read 2026-09-29.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu, per the photographer's Wikimedia Commons user page), via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px
images.license_note: Wikimedia Commons' license box on the file page confirms CC0 (public domain dedication) by the author Firstcultural; the author's Commons user page (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:Firstcultural) gives the name Alfred Twu. File page read 2026-09-23, user page read 2026-09-29.
images.caption: Aerial photo of San Francisco's Mission Bay, ballpark, and Caltrain area
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

open_questions: Precise completion month in 2009 is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year.

DataSF Assessor's own use_code/unit-count fields for this specific parcel (Single Family Residential, 0 units, 2 stories) look like a condo common-element or garage lot rather than the full building, while listing sites describe a larger residential building at this address; not reconciled here.
Unit count for this address alone (as distinct from the combined 131-unit BMR program across both 330 and 335 Berry St) is not confirmed from a single source.
Developer/architect not confirmed from any source checked as of 2026-09-29.

Whether the 131 BMR units were actually allocated by the scheduled January 28, 2009 lottery, and which program they were sold under, are not stated by any source checked: SocketSite's post announces the lottery and names neither the program nor the Redevelopment Agency.
